standards-1.text: [important] `skills/wiki-cycle/SKILL.md` (the `--resume` paragraph), `skills/wiki-report/SKILL.md` (`## Fallbacks`), `skills/wiki-report/wiki-seed/wiki-report.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` (the 2026-11-15 entry): the docs say different things about when `not checked` appears. SKILL.md says "A resumed run does not create `fallbacks.txt` unless a step has a fallback to record". The report SKILL says "the file is absent: `Fallbacks: not checked (no fallbacks.txt in the run folder)`, never `none`". The seed says "or "Fallbacks: not checked" for a run begun before the rule". The CHANGELOG says "A run resumed from before this change reports `Fallbacks: not checked`". Under the SKILL rules, any resumed run after this change with nothing to record also reads `not checked`, so the seed and CHANGELOG narrow the label to runs "begun before the rule". The wording is Mark's choice (plan confirmation, 2026-11-15), so only the docs are wrong. Fix: make the seed and CHANGELOG say "any run folder with no `fallbacks.txt`" (a resumed run included). Rule: doc accuracy, no rule code.

standards-2.text: [important] `skills/wiki-cycle/SKILL.md` (the YouTube bullet and the worker-note bullet): two note forms exist for a worker's fallback. The YouTube bullet names "`Fallback: transcribed`". `skills/wiki-update/fetchers.md` prints `Fallback: transcribed (subtitles HTTP 429)`. The worker rule asks for "`Fallback: expected X; used Y; why Z`", and the orchestrator copies only that form. The one fetcher fallback the skill names does not fit the copy rule, which is the miss lesson #12 is about. Fix: state one note form in SKILL.md and say how the fetcher's printed line maps to it. Rule: skill-prose contradiction.

standards-3.text: [important] PY9, `tests/skills/wiki-cycle/check.py`: `FB_BRIEF = re.compile(r"fallback.{0,250}?\bnotes?\b|\bnotes?\b.{0,250}?fallback", re.I | re.S)`, used by "every wiki-ingester worker's brief tells it to name any fallback in its Notes". It passes any brief where the words "fallback" and "notes" sit within 250 characters, without the `expected` / `used` / `why` sentence. Fix: match `Fallback: expected` plus `used` and `why`. Same family: `FB_DEFAULT_MODEL = re.compile(r"\bdefault\b|\bsonnet\b", re.I)` passes on the word "default" anywhere in the setting-file line, including the why field. Fix: test the model field only. The Spec lens raised the `FB_BRIEF` point separately; the two lenses agree.

spec-1.text: [important] `tests/skills/wiki-cycle/` (process, the Step 9 edit): the plan's honour rule was broken for the Step 9 reorder, and the reason given for the edit does not hold. Intent: plan.md:41, "the session that edits the skill does not read `cases.json` while it edits (honour rule)". Implemented: checkpoints.md:35, "this edit was made by a session that had read cases.json", justified as touching "only the Step 9 order, which no new case's check reads". The check that drove the edit was "nothing left uncommitted in the notebook", which every new case carries (baseline-opus.json:863 and :919, and the same key in older cases). Affected: the claim that the reorder fixed the resumed case on Opus (run 20261115-145233) rests on an edit by a session that had read the case file, and the claim that it is test-neutral is unsupported. Fix: record the deviation in the PENDING.md row and in checkpoints.md, then re-run the resumed case on Opus after an edit by a session that has not read cases.json, or have Mark accept the deviation in writing.

standards-23.text: [important] PY9 / R15, `tests/skills/wiki-cycle/check.py:2514` and `:2570`: the Notes requirement is unanchored, so the check name overstates what it tests. The check is named "every wiki-ingester worker's brief tells it to name any fallback in its Notes". `FB_NOTES = re.compile(r"\bnotes\b", re.I)` is applied to the whole prompt: `return bool(FB_BRIEF.search(prompt) and FB_NOTES.search(prompt))`. A brief that drops the Notes instruction still passes if "notes" appears elsewhere in it. Fix: require the shape and `Notes` in one line or sentence (a bounded window), or rename the check (the name is pinned by the baselines). Reviewer's note: round 2 asked for "a `Notes` requirement to the same test" and this is that fix as written, so the finding is the fix's weakness, not a missed request. The lens could not tell whether a real worker brief mentions "notes" elsewhere (unverified below). The Spec lens raised the same point as a suggestion; the two labels are kept apart.

spec-10.text: [suggestion] `tests/skills/wiki-cycle/check.py:2659`: the check name says each worker's brief tells it to name fallbacks "in its Notes", but the test needs only the shape and the word "Notes" somewhere in the prompt (`check.py:2570`). Intent: `plan.md:106`, "every `wiki-ingester` worker's brief tells it to name any fallback in its Notes"; `requirements.md:52` (Decision 5), "the worker's brief says to name any fallback it used in the receipt's Notes column". Code: `FB_NOTES = re.compile(r"\bnotes\b", re.I)` (`check.py:2514`); nothing binds Notes to the sentence. The shipped sentence at `SKILL.md:110` has both in one clause, so a false pass is narrow. Affected: the suite's only automated proof of the worker-brief step. Fix: one line or sentence for both, or rename. A partial close of round 2's Spec 4 on this point; the same defect as the Standards `important`, labelled by this lens as a suggestion.

spec-11.text: [suggestion] `skills/wiki-cycle/wiki-seed/wiki-cycle.md:51` (new this round): "a resumed run where nothing fell back also reads \"not checked\", since resuming does not create the file". Intent: `plan.md:26` puts "a rule-era run resumed after its Step 0 with nothing found since" under the absent-file label, but `SKILL.md:53` has Step 0 create `fallbacks.txt`. Code: a rule-era run keeps its header-only file, and `skills/wiki-report/SKILL.md:271` reads that as `Fallbacks: none`. The clause is true only for a run begun before the rule; as written, "a resumed run" is broader. Affected: a reader interpreting a resumed run's report. Fix: limit the clause to runs begun before the rule, or cut it; reconcile `plan.md:26` with `SKILL.md:53`.

The plan's rule is written for the note, so applying it to the brief is an inference. Fix: drop the allowance if the rule binds the brief too.
